overview.allGood: The advisor's rules found nothing to fix.
overview.partial: The picture is partial: cloud sessions, other machines and transcripts older than 30 days before quipu was installed are not included.
overview.empty.title: No sessions in this period yet
overview.empty.body: Quipu collects Claude Code transcripts in the background. Work in Claude Code, or pick a longer period.
khipu.label: Khipu of your projects
khipu.legend: Each cord is a project. Colour and length show cache writes, and the knots record the number the way Inca khipus did: thousands, hundreds, tens and units of {unit} tokens from top to bottom. A red side cord marks things worth fixing; its knot counts them.
khipu.more: Showing {shown} of {total} projects, those with the most cache writes; the rest are in the list below.
stat.cacheWritesNote: what uses up your limits most
stat.missesNote: with a reason from the API
finding.applyNote: quipu keeps a copy of the files first: undo right in the notification, or later under Advice, in “Changes made by quipu”.
finding.manual: This one needs a manual edit: it takes your judgement.
rule.large-import.title: @{ref} adds ≈ {tokens} tokens to every session
rule.large-import.detail: An @import loads the whole file at the start of every session, even when the task does not need it. Mention it in plain text and say when to read it; Claude opens it when it is needed.

rule.claude-ai-skills.title.one: {count} skill from claude.ai adds ≈ {tokens} tokens to every session
rule.claude-ai-skills.title.other: {count} skills from claude.ai add ≈ {tokens} tokens to every session

rule.claude-ai-skills.detail: These skills are synced from claude.ai and listed in every session of every project: {names}. The change hides them from the model; they stay available as /name. To stop syncing them entirely, set "syncClaudeAiSkills": false.
rule.long-claude-md.title: {name} has {lines} lines (recommended up to {limit})
rule.long-claude-md.detail: The whole file is sent with every request. Move topic-specific rules to .claude/rules/*.md with paths:, and step-by-step procedures to skills.
rule.memory-limit.title.over: MEMORY.md has {lines} lines; only the first {limit} are loaded
rule.memory-limit.title: MEMORY.md is nearly full
rule.memory-limit.detail.over: Claude does not see entries past the limit. Merge similar ones and remove stale ones.
rule.memory-limit.detail.near: New entries will soon be cut off. Merge similar ones and remove stale ones.

rule.repeated-in-session.title.one: {name} repeats {count} line your CLAUDE.md already sends
rule.repeated-in-session.title.other: {name} repeats {count} lines your CLAUDE.md already sends

rule.repeated-in-session.detail: Every session of this project gets these lines twice: from your settings and from the project file. Remove the project copy; your settings keep sending them.

rule.shared-block.title.one: A block of {lines} lines is copied into {count} project: “{first}”
rule.shared-block.title.other: A block of {lines} lines is copied into {count} projects: “{first}”

rule.shared-block.detail.some: Each copy has to be updated by hand. Keep one in your CLAUDE.md and remove it from the projects. It is then also sent in the other projects of this profile ({others}), ≈ {tokens} tokens each.
rule.shared-block.detail.all: Each copy has to be updated by hand. Every project of this profile already has the block, so keep it once in your CLAUDE.md: no extra tokens, and one place to change it.
rule.copied-extension.detail.skill: The copies are identical. In one click quipu moves one to ~/.claude/skills/{name}/ (skills there work in every project) and deletes the others, so it is changed in one place.
rule.copied-extension.detail.rule: The copies are identical. In one click quipu moves one to ~/.claude/rules/ (rules there apply in every project) and deletes the others, so it is changed in one place.
rule.copied-extension.detail.agent: The copies are identical. In one click quipu moves one to ~/.claude/agents/ (agents there work in every project) and deletes the others, so it is changed in one place.
project.startTitle: What is sent at the start of a session
project.alwaysNote: These files and descriptions go into every request.
project.onDemandNote: Loaded only when Claude touches matching files or invokes a skill.
context.aria: Session start: Claude Code {claude}, your files {files}
advice.title: Advice
advice.subtitle: What to change so Claude Code sends less that it does not need
advice.userNote: One change applies to every project.
cache.title: Cache and tokens
cache.subtitle: Where your limits go and why the cache misses
cache.missesNote: The API reports these reasons itself, so they are not guesses.
miss.previous_message_not_found: The cache expired after a pause
miss.previous_message_not_found.tip: After a long break, start a new session or /clear instead of continuing the old one.
miss.messages_changed: Part of the conversation already sent changed
miss.messages_changed.tip: Happens after /compact or when earlier messages are edited.
miss.system_changed.tip: CLAUDE.md, settings or the output style changed mid-session.
miss.tools_changed.tip: An MCP server or plugin was connected or turned off mid-session.
miss.model_changed.tip: Pick the model at the start of a session: switching resets the cache.
profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.subtitle: Separate Claude accounts, such as personal and work, and which folders run under which
profiles.name: Name
profiles.nameNote: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. The profile lives in ~/.claude-name.
profiles.shareNote: Projects, memory and transcripts are never shared, so personal and work stay apart.
profiles.removeNote: The profile folder with its login and sessions stays on disk; quipu removes only its own links and settings.
rules.title: Which folder uses which profile
rules.note: quipu run starts Claude under the profile of the nearest folder with a rule.
rules.empty: No rules yet: everything runs as default, and quipu run asks.
signin.title: Sign in to {name}
signin.why: If the browser is already signed in to claude.ai with another account, the sign-in page just confirms that one. That is why quipu opens it in a private window.
signin.emailNote: Optional: Claude fills it in on the sign-in page.
signin.start: Sign in in a private window
signin.step.open: The sign-in page is ready. If no private window opened, open it one of these ways:
signin.step.wait: Sign in with the right account; this panel updates by itself.
auth.title: Open quipu through its link
auth.body: Only the link with a token can open this page. Run in a terminal:
notFound.title: There is no such page
result.applied: Applied. Open Claude Code sessions see the change after /clear.
result.undone: Undone: the files are back as they were.
result.finding-gone: This finding is gone or cannot be applied automatically. The page was refreshed.
result.file-changed: Not applied: {path} changed after the finding was made. Check it and try again.
result.undo-changed: Not undone: the file was edited after quipu changed it, and undoing would lose that edit.
result.project-unknown: No such project among the collected ones.
result.profile-added: Profile {name} created in {dir}. Now sign in to it.
result.profile-removed: Profile {name} removed. Its folder with the login stays: {dir}
result.folder-not-absolute: Give the full path to the folder, or a path starting with ~/.
result.rule-saved: Claude in {folder} and below now runs as {name}.
result.email-invalid: That does not look like an email address.
result.sign-in-private: The sign-in page opened in a private window: sign in there with the account for {name}.
result.private-window-failed: Could not open a private window: copy the link and paste it into one yourself.
result.unauthorized: No access: open quipu with quipu ui.
settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: How quipu looks, Remote Control, the claude shim and a check of the setup
editor.title: Editor
editor.newFile: The file does not exist yet: saving creates it.
editor.conflict: The file changed outside the editor. Reload it so those changes are not overwritten.
editor.hint: Ctrl+S saves; undo in the notification or under Changes
project.noChanges: quipu has not changed this project's files yet.
result.saved: Saved. Open Claude Code sessions see the change after /clear.
result.file-not-editable: quipu does not edit this file: {path}
result.file-too-big: The file is too big for the editor: {path}
rule.edit.title: Edited in quipu
rule.copied-extension.detail.exists: Your settings already have a different “{name}”, so quipu does not move anything itself. Compare them and keep one.
live.title: Claude Code sessions now
live.note: Running claude processes on this computer.
live.unknownHint: Remote Control turned on with /remote-control cannot be seen from outside.
live.autoStart: Claude Code's settings turn Remote Control on for every session (remoteControlAtStartup).

live.banner.title.one: Remote Control is on in {count} session
live.banner.title.other: Remote Control is on in {count} sessions

live.banner.howOff: This session can be driven from claude.ai or the phone. To turn it off, type /remote-control in it again or close it.
settings.rc.title: Remote Control
settings.rc.note: quipu sees sessions started with Remote Control (claude --rc, claude remote-control). When it is turned on with /remote-control in an open session, only a hook can tell: it goes into Claude Code's settings and on every prompt records for quipu whether Remote Control is connected. The hook prints nothing into the session.
settings.rc.toggle: Watch Remote Control (add a hook to Claude Code's settings)
settings.rc.on: The hook is in place. Remove it here or undo it under Changes.
settings.rc.off: No hook; only sessions started with Remote Control are seen.
result.watching-on: Watching Remote Control. New and open sessions report from their next prompt.
result.watching-off: Stopped watching Remote Control; the hook is removed.
result.no-self-binary: Could not tell where quipu is installed, to put it into the hook.
rule.watch-remote-control.title: Remote Control watching
backup.title: Backup
backup.subtitle: The Claude Code setup of every profile: save it, and get it back after a reinstall or on a new computer
backup.what: CLAUDE.md, settings.json, rules, skills (not the ones synced from claude.ai), agents, commands, project memory and quipu's profiles. Credentials, transcripts and caches are never included; before saving, quipu looks for keys and tokens in the files.
backup.gitLabel: Or into a private git repository
backup.gitNote: A folder with a clone of your private repository; if there is none yet, quipu creates a local repository. quipu commits itself and pushes only when ticked, using your own git setup.
backup.secretsTitle: The files seem to contain credentials, so nothing was saved:
backup.secretsNote: Most often these are keys in the env block of settings.json. Remove them there, or save anyway if the copy stays only with you.
backup.restoreNote: Before writing, quipu shows what is new and what changes; a restore is undone in one click.

backup.previewLinks.one: {count} link shared between profiles is also created.
backup.previewLinks.other: {count} links shared between profiles are also created.

backup.applyNote: quipu keeps a copy of the current files; undo in the notification or under Changes.
result.backup-unchanged: Nothing changed in {path} since the last save.
result.restored: Restored. Open Claude Code sessions see the changes after /clear.
rule.restore.title: Restored from a backup
project.pluginsNote: Enabled for this project: their skills, agents and commands are listed in every session. Their MCP tools cost tokens too, but only Claude Code knows how many.
rule.unused-plugin.title: Plugin {name} was not used in 30 days
rule.unused-plugin.detail.user: It is enabled for every project, so its skills, agents, commands and MCP tools are in every session of every project. Turn it off; enable it again when you need it.
rule.unused-plugin.detail.project: It is enabled in the project's settings, so it is in every session of this project. Turn it off; enable it again when you need it.
rule.unused-plugin.detail.local: It is enabled in your local project settings, so it is in every session of this project. Turn it off; enable it again when you need it.
rule.plugin-one-project.title: Plugin {name} is enabled for every project but used only in {project}
rule.plugin-one-project.detail: Now it is in every session of every project. In one click quipu turns it off in your general settings and on for {project} only (in settings.local.json, just for you); the other projects ({others}) stop paying for it.
settings.shim.title: The claude shim
settings.shim.note: Then the plain claude command picks the account by the folder rules, without quipu run. The real claude is not touched: quipu puts its own folder first on PATH with one line in your shell's startup file.
settings.shim.on: On: new terminals pick the profile by folder (line in {file}).
settings.shim.half: The link is there, but the line in {file} is not, so terminals do not see it.
doctor.title: Check
doctor.claude.fix: Install Claude Code: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
doctor.installs.warn: Several different claude programs on PATH: {list}
doctor.installs.fix: Keep one install, so different terminals do not run different versions.
doctor.login.fix: Sign in on the Profiles page or with quipu profile login {name}.
doctor.broken-link.fix: The file it points to is gone. Remove the link or bring the file back.
doctor.rule-profile.fail: The rule for {folder} points to profile {name}, which does not exist
doctor.rule-profile.fix: Change or remove the rule on the Profiles page.
doctor.rule-folder.warn: The rule for {folder} (profile {name}): the folder is gone
doctor.rule-folder.fix: Remove the rule on the Profiles page if the folder is no longer needed.
doctor.shim.warn: The claude shim is installed but not on PATH
doctor.shim.fix: Turn it on with the button above: quipu adds the line to {rc}.
doctor.shim.info: The claude shim is off; quipu run picks the profile by folder
doctor.daemon.ok: The quipu service runs and collects history
doctor.daemon.warn: The quipu service is not running: history is not collected while quipu is closed
doctor.daemon.fix: Run quipu install to start the service with the system.
doctor.window.info: The quipu window is not installed; the interface opens in the browser
doctor.window.warn: The quipu window does not start
doctor.window.fix: WebKitGTK is missing: sudo apt install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 (Debian, Ubuntu) or sudo dnf install webkit2gtk4.1 (Fedora).
doctor.rc-autostart.warn: Remote Control turns on in every session (remoteControlAtStartup)
doctor.rc-autostart.fix: If that is not on purpose, turn off “Enable Remote Control for all sessions” in Claude Code's /config.
result.shim-on: The claude shim is on. Open a new terminal.
rule.shim.title: The claude shim
new.title: New project
new.subtitle: Set up a new or freshly cloned project with your own skills, rules and agents, and see what Claude will read before anything is written.
new.name: Name
new.summaryHint: One or two sentences; you can write it later in CLAUDE.md.
new.noExtensions: Your projects have no skills, rules or agents of their own yet.
new.next: Start Claude Code in it; once there is code, run /init to add its commands to CLAUDE.md:
new.undoNote: Undo it in the toast or under Advice, in “Changes made by quipu”: the files and any move to global are reverted together.
new.ruleError: The files are written, but the profile rule was not saved; set it on the Profiles page.
result.extension-missing: {path} is gone or is not a skill, rule or agent.
rule.new-project.title: New project {name}
new.step1Hint: A new folder, or one you just cloned: files already there are kept as they are. Commands come later: once there is code, /init in Claude Code adds them to CLAUDE.md.
new.step3Hint: One click writes everything; one click in Changes undoes it.
new.startLabel: Every session of this project starts with
new.group.alwaysHint: Paid at the start of every conversation, so it stays short.
new.group.demandHint: Loaded only when Claude touches matching files or runs the skill.
new.group.unreadHint: Files Claude does not load by itself.
new.about.claude-md: The project's name and purpose; /init fills in the rest once there is code.
new.about.skill: A procedure Claude follows on request; only its description is always listed.
new.about.agent: A helper Claude can hand a task to.
new.about.rule: A rule you wrote; with paths: it loads only for matching files.
new.existingFolder: This folder already exists: quipu adds only the files it does not have.
new.step2Hint: Skills, rules and agents you already wrote. What several projects share is better made global than copied again.
new.variants: {count} different versions; the most recently changed one is used
new.globalNote: Moves to your own settings and works in every project, this one included; the copies in projects are removed. One version to keep up to date.
new.copyNote: Makes copy number {count}; the advice will suggest merging them later.
new.nothingNew: The folder already has everything chosen; pick something to add.
new.kept: already in the folder, kept as it is
new.movedGlobal: made global: works in every project
result.not-a-folder: {folder} is a file, not a folder.
result.nothing-new: Nothing to add: the folder already has these files.
result.global-gone: {path} can no longer be made global (the copies changed); copy it instead.
collect.title: Reading your Claude Code history
collect.body: The first time, quipu goes through every session transcript once. Later it reads only what changed, in the background.
settings.shim.shellsNote: The line goes into your login shell's startup file. A terminal that runs another shell, such as the one in PhpStorm or VS Code (often zsh), needs it in that shell's file too.
settings.shim.newTerminal: The change applies to terminals opened after it; in an IDE, open a new terminal tab.
result.shim-rc-on: Added the line to {file}. Open a new terminal.
result.shell-unknown: quipu does not know the shell {shell}.
rules.shim: To make plain claude pick the profile by these rules, turn on
profiles.statusHint: Shows the profile, context use and this account's 5-hour and weekly limits under the prompt.
rules.memoryShared: Memory is shared with {from}: both accounts read and add to it.
rules.memoryOther: {from} has memory of this project ({count} files) that {name} does not see.
result.statusline-on: {name} shows the quipu status line from its next session.
result.statusline-off: {name} no longer shows the quipu status line.
result.memory-unshared: {name} has its own memory of {folder} again, starting from a copy.
result.memory-none: No other profile has memory for this project.
result.memory-conflict: Both accounts have different {files}; keep one and try again.
rule.statusline.title: quipu status line for {name}
rule.share-memory.title: Shared the memory of {project} with {name}
rule.unshare-memory.title: Stopped sharing the memory of {project} with {name}
